newsitem.title: IRAQ: Allied base in north Iraq moved to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Allied base in north Iraq moved to Turkey.

text.p: Allied military personnel based in the northern town of Zakho began evacuating the area on Tuesday, hours before U.S. cruise missiles slammed into Iraqi military targets in the south of the country, witnesses said.

A member of the United Nations guards contingent, stationed in the area, said soldiers attached to the Zakho quarters of the U.S.-led Operation Provide Comfort (OPC) had moved across the border to Silopi, in Turkey.
"Personnel from OPC and refugees have left for the border," an U.N. guard told Reuters. He said around 50 Turkish Kurds had also been taken across the border to Turkey.
Kurdish sources in the region said they had gone to Silopi in Turkey's border province of Sirnak.
Lou Boone, European command spokesman in Stuttgart, told Reuters: "We began to evacuate some of the personnel, and select non-governmental organisations just before the attack."
Around 100 people had already left Iraq in the evacuation begun at around 0300 GMT, and the rest were in transit, he said.
British embassy sources said similar evacuations were underway for their nationals.

A military source in the U.S. base in Incirlik in southern Turkey said the cruise missile attacks had no effect on OPC patrols over the region. Witnesses said flight activity from Incirlik appeared to be normal.
OPC was set up after the 1991 Gulf War to protect Iraqi Kurds from Baghdad's attacks.
